_comment: Routes for the flight watch bot. Add or remove them in the UI: python check.py --ui

budget._cap_note: SerpApi free tier is 250 searches/month. ONE SEARCH = ONE DATE PAIR - the google_flights engine has no flexible-date mode, so a run samples dates rather than covering a range. The bot refuses to start a run that would breach this.
budget._runs_note: Weekly schedule = 4.3 runs/month. Matches .github/workflows/check-flights.yml. Sampling density is derived from these two numbers, so you never set step size by hand.

defaults._note: Shared by every route. These barely ever change, which is why they live here once instead of being repeated on each watch.

window._note: How far ahead to look. 300 is the booking horizon - airlines haven't loaded schedules past it, so searches there return nothing and still cost a credit.

defaults._stops_note: 0 = any, 1 = nonstop only, 2 = 1 stop or fewer, 3 = 2 stops or fewer. Set to 1 on 24 Aug 2026: a BNE-Tokyo connection runs 20-25h against ~9h nonstop, so a cheap connecting fare is not really the same product. WATCH OUT: in the first live run, zero BNE-HND results were nonstop - if that route has no direct service, every HND search returns nothing and still costs a credit.
defaults._level_note: The only alerting rule. Google's own verdict, built on real price history for this route and these dates, and it recalibrates by season on its own. 'low' means roughly 'below the floor of the typical range', so it is a high bar - expect quiet weeks. Add 'typical' if you want far more noise.

notify._cooldown_note: null = never email the same date pair twice, however many runs go by. Set hours instead to be reminded periodically about a fare that's still cheap.
notify._renotify_note: The one exception: if the price fell another this-many % since the last alert, it gets through. Being told twice about the same fare is noise; a further drop is new information.

watches._note: Use a REAL airport code. The TYO metro code is accepted by the API but returns zero flights - verified live. NRT (Narita) is where the budget carriers fly; HND (Haneda) is closer to central Tokyo.

watches._stops_note: Overrides the nonstop default. Verified live on 24 Aug 2026: BNE-HND returns ZERO results with stops=1, so nonstop-only would spend a credit per date and get nothing back. 2 = one stop or fewer, which keeps the sane connections and drops the two-stop marathons.
